## Equivalent rational expression

The prompt states the domain (x\ne -n). A cancelled fraction and the original unreduced expression both receive full credit because the question asks for *any equivalent expression* on that domain. A reciprocal triggers a targeted feedback branch.

```{.stack-question}
#| file: questions/rational-equivalence.xml
#| question: Equivalent rational expression
#| variants: 3
#| seed: 29
#| review: true
#| feedback: true
#| label: rational-practice
#| feedback-policy: two-step-practice
```

[Download the rational question](questions/rational-equivalence.xml)

This activity selects `two-step-practice`: a guiding question followed by a worked
explanation. Its named parents inherit the shared mathematics instructions and
set a 90-word limit. The other feedback activities on this page inherit the
shared four-step sequence with the same page limit. See the
[policy setup](docs/authoring.qmd#choose-a-teaching-policy) to adapt it.

## Three numerical checks

These fields demonstrate absolute tolerance, relative tolerance, and decimal-place precision. The final field distinguishes `17.5` from `17.50`, because the written precision is part of the task. Their response trees contribute 30%, 40%, and 30% of the total.

::: {#measurement-context .ai-context}
For a measured quantity, absolute tolerance compares $|x-a|$ to a fixed bound. Relative tolerance compares it to a fraction of the reference value. Written decimal places express the precision of a reported measurement.
:::

```{.stack-question}
#| file: questions/numerical-measurement.xml
#| question: Rectangle and triangle measurements
#| seed: 47
#| review: true
#| feedback: true
#| context: measurement-context
```

[Download the numerical question](questions/numerical-measurement.xml)

## Find a nonidentity matrix with determinant one

Enter **any integer $2\times2$ matrix with determinant 1, except the identity**.
This adapts the [math-exercise matrix-constraint example](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/math-exercise/custom-assessment.html).
Each of the three conditions earns one third of the score: integer entries,
determinant one, and nonidentity. You are finding a matrix that satisfies
conditions, rather than copying a displayed model answer.

```{#determinant-one .stack-question}
#| file: questions/determinant-one.xml
#| question: A nonidentity integer matrix with determinant one
#| seed: 17
#| review: true
#| feedback: true
#| context: none
```

[Download XML](questions/determinant-one.xml) · [Original source and conversion record](questions/determinant-example-provenance.json)

**For STACK authors:** this keeps the source exercise’s three conditions and
partial credit, using three normal response trees. The new Python-only
`MatrixProperty` test checks each condition; the XML is not a drop-in native
STACK question. In native STACK, author equivalent Maxima calculations and
response-tree checks. See [Python answer tests](docs/python-answer-tests.qmd)
for this distinction and [matrix input](docs/matrix-input.qmd) for input limits.

## Matrix problems from INGMat 3A

These three questions adapt Andrey Chesnokov’s [week 3, section 3.8](https://aacchhee.github.io/ingmat3a_ntnu/pages/uke3.html#uke3-stotte-oppgaver), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. The original math-exercise blocks and exact source revision are in the [source record](questions/course-examples-provenance.json).

### Rank and pivot columns: ordinary STACK answer tests

usual STACK grading structure; it does not use the basis helper.

```{#course-b-rank-pivots .stack-question}

#| question: Rank and pivot columns of B
#| seed: 17
#| review: true
```

### A basis for the null space of B

**Python extension: `IsBasis`.** Put one proposed basis vector in each column.
A basis is not a unique matrix: changing a vector’s nonzero scale can still
give a correct answer. Choose the number of columns before validating.

```{#course-b-nullspace .stack-question}
#| file: questions/course-b-nullspace.xml
#| question: A basis for the null space of B
#| seed: 17
#| review: true
```

[Download XML](questions/course-b-nullspace.xml)

### A basis for the null space of C

**Python extension: `IsBasis`.** Here you may also reorder or mix the reference
basis vectors, provided your columns remain independent and span the same
null space. Entry-by-entry equality with one model matrix would reject many
correct answers, so this question uses a basis test instead.

```{#course-c-nullspace .stack-question}
#| file: questions/course-c-nullspace.xml
#| question: A basis for the null space of C
#| seed: 17
#| review: true
```

[Download XML](questions/course-c-nullspace.xml)

For both basis questions, **green** means that the submitted nonzero columns
are in the target space and form an independent family among the valid columns; red columns are excluded from that diagnostic independence check. A green family can
still be incomplete. **Yellow** marks every column of a dependent valid family;
column order never decides which vector gets the blame. **Red** marks a zero
vector or one outside the target space. The complete answer receives credit
only when it is a basis; colors do not award partial credit. Edits and resizing
clear the colors and require validation again.

The basis questions extend vanilla STACK: they keep the familiar XML inputs and
PRTs but introduce a Python-only answer test. The resizable matrix input is
also a port extension. Read [how the Python extension works, and what the XML
means in native STACK](docs/python-answer-tests.qmd).


## Custom Python checker {#custom-python-checker}

An author module can define a new predicate without editing this extension.
This example accepts any positive integer multiple of the displayed number.
The XML chooses `PythonChecker`, the authored block selects its module, and
the usual response tree awards credit. See the [version 1 API](docs/python-checker-api.qmd)
for the callable contract, immutable values, tests and portability.

```{.stack-question #python-multiple}
#| file: questions/python-checker.xml
#| question: A positive integer multiple (PythonChecker)
#| python-checkers: questions/checkers.py
#| variants: 3
#| seed: 17
#| review: true
```
